items.headline: Opposition politician Lim Tean ordered to begin a three-month jail term on July 20
items.summary: The Court of Appeal refused Lim Tean, 61, leave to challenge his enhanced sentence, ordering him to surrender on July 20 to serve three months and one week for practising law without a valid certificate.

items.headline: Aperia Group CEO charged with laundering S$38m via a bungalow in Nvidia-chips fraud case
items.summary: Alan Wei Zhaolun, 50, pleaded not guilty to 11 charges including laundering S$38m through a S$55m Good Class Bungalow, tied to routing Nvidia-chip servers out of Singapore against US export controls.

items.headline: Singapore marriages fell 6.2% in 2025, but most couples report being happy
items.summary: An MSF Family Trends Report showed civil marriages fell from 21,144 to 19,682; divorce before the 10th anniversary dropped to 13.5% for the 2014 cohort and 94.9% said they were happy.

items.headline: New bill proposes up to 15 years' jail for purposeful endangerment with a vehicle
items.summary: The Road Traffic (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill, introduced July 7, creates an offence of purposeful endangerment using a vehicle causing death or grievous hurt, carrying up to 15 years' jail.

items.headline: Baruipur child rape-murder ignites a BJP-TMC clash after a suspect dies in police custody
items.summary: The rape-murder of a girl of about 11-12 in Baruipur triggered mob violence and the police-custody shooting of suspect Prabhas Mondol on July 7, sparking a BJP-TMC war in West Bengal.

items.headline: RBI faces a $100 billion challenge unwinding its record rupee-defence position
items.summary: India's central bank must unwind a short-dollar forward book that hit a record $106.7bn in May after intervening to defend the rupee; with rates at 5.25%, it has begun trimming carefully.

items.headline: Milky Mist Dairy plans India's largest dairy-sector IPO at about $213 million
items.summary: Tamil Nadu-based Milky Mist Dairy Food is preparing a 20.35 billion rupee (about $213m) IPO as early as late July, set to be India's largest dairy-sector share sale.

items.headline: India's IT majors head into earnings under AI and Middle East pressure
items.summary: HCL Technologies, Wipro and Tech Mahindra report quarterly results as investors question traditional IT services in the AI era amid Middle East uncertainty.

items.headline: Andy Burnham on course to become UK PM after 322 of 403 Labour MPs back him
items.summary: On the first day of nominations to replace Keir Starmer, Andy Burnham secured 322 of 403 Labour MPs, all but assuring an unopposed win and a July 20 appointment as PM.

items.headline: Nigel Farage resigns as an MP amid a funding scandal, forcing a Clacton by-election
items.summary: Farage quit his Clacton seat on July 7 after revelations about undisclosed backing including a reported £5m from Christopher Harborne; he intends to re-stand.

items.headline: Police open an investigation into donations to Reform UK
items.summary: Detectives are examining Farage-linked donations, including two £250,000 gifts by Fiona Cottrell and the roughly £5m from Christopher Harborne.

items.headline: Main UK parties say they will boycott Farage's Clacton by-election
items.summary: Labour, the Conservatives and the Liberal Democrats will not field candidates in the by-election; Kemi Badenoch called it a 'fake' contest and Ed Davey a 'vanity project'.

items.headline: Update: Trump declares the US-Iran ceasefire 'over' as Washington adds fresh sanctions
items.summary: Trump said the ceasefire is over even as he agreed to keep talking, imposing new sanctions on Tehran after Iranian fire on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz; Qatar and Pakistan pushed to revive talks.

items.headline: US senators reach a deal with the Trump administration to advance a Russia sanctions bill
items.summary: Senators Graham, Blumenthal, Wicker and Shaheen agreed with the administration to move a package letting Trump impose heavy tariffs on buyers of Russian oil, gas and uranium.

items.headline: US charges gangster Lawrence Bishnoi over the 2023 assassination of activist Hardeep Singh Nijjar
items.summary: A Los Angeles indictment charges Lawrence Bishnoi, 33, and 'Goldy Brar' with ordering the June 2023 killing of Hardeep Singh Nijjar in Surrey, BC; the case names 37 defendants.

items.headline: China expands its anti-sanctions toolkit, raising risks for foreign firms
items.summary: Beijing is rolling out new legal measures to widen retaliation against US and EU sanctions and export controls, raising compliance risks amid EU-China trade tensions.

items.headline: Israeli strikes kill at least nine in Gaza despite the ceasefire, including an aid worker
items.summary: Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least nine Palestinians in 24 hours despite the truce, among them a World Central Kitchen driver and four killed in a strike on a tent in al-Mawasi.

items.headline: Apple sues OpenAI, alleging a coordinated theft of trade secrets for AI hardware
items.summary: Apple sued OpenAI in the Northern District of California for misappropriating trade secrets to build its first AI hardware device, naming former staff Chang Liu and Tang Tan.

items.headline: Big Tech has doubled its debt load to about $350 billion in the AI spending spree
items.summary: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle have added roughly $350bn in debt over five years to fund the AI build-out, doubling their combined debt load.

items.headline: Paris voice-AI startup Gradium raises a $100 million seed round backed by Nvidia
items.summary: Gradium reopened its seed round to new investors including Nvidia, bringing the total to $100m — an unusually large seed underscoring the rush into voice-AI infrastructure.

items.headline: Hugging Face's CEO says companies are done renting their AI
items.summary: CEO Clem Delangue argues open-source AI is booming as enterprises shift from renting closed models to self-hosting, citing use by roughly half the Fortune 500.

items.headline: SK Hynix raises $26.5 billion in the largest-ever US listing by a foreign company
items.summary: SK Hynix priced 177.9m ADRs at $149 to raise $26.5bn, topping Alibaba's 2014 IPO as the biggest US debut by a non-American firm; the stock popped about 14% on Nasdaq.

items.headline: Circle wins final OCC approval for a national trust bank, and its shares surge
items.summary: Circle received final OCC approval to establish Circle National Trust, letting it directly custody the reserves backing USDC; shares jumped as much as 14%.

items.headline: Apollo trumps Castlelake with a £5.7bn bid for easyJet, and shares jump
items.summary: Apollo offered 715p a share for easyJet, valuing it at about £5.7bn and beating Castlelake's 690p deal; easyJet is 'no longer minded to recommend' Castlelake and shares rose about 13%.

items.headline: Xavier Niel becomes Vodafone's biggest shareholder in a $6 billion deal
items.summary: UAE's e& agreed to sell its ~16% Vodafone stake to a vehicle controlled by Xavier Niel for about $6bn (~112.5p a share); Vodafone shares rose about 13%.

items.headline: Wall Street ends the week higher as tech leads; S&P 500 gains 0.4% on Friday
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.42% to 7,575.39, the Nasdaq added 0.29% to 26,281.61 and the Dow gained 0.29% to 52,637.01, capping a winning week led by Nvidia and Meta.

items.headline: 🎾 Sinner beats Djokovic in straight sets to reach the Wimbledon final
items.summary: World No. 1 Jannik Sinner beat Novak Djokovic 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 to reach Sunday's final against Alexander Zverev, who beat Arthur Fery; Sinner chases back-to-back titles.

items.headline: 🎾 An all-Czech Wimbledon women's final guarantees a first-time champion
items.summary: Karolina Muchova and Linda Noskova meet in an all-Czech Wimbledon final; Muchova saved a match point to beat Coco Gauff and Noskova beat Marta Kostyuk.

items.headline: 🏏 England eye a 4-0 sweep as a winless India seek pride in the 5th T20I
items.summary: England, 3-0 up and unassailable, aim for a 4-0 whitewash in the fifth T20I at Southampton; a win lifts them above India in the ICC T20I rankings, with India winless under Shreyas Iyer.

items.headline: 🏎️ Verstappen's 2027 market heats up as McLaren becomes the last top seat
items.summary: With a contract clause set to activate if Verstappen is outside the top two by the summer break, his 2027 future dominates the paddock; Mercedes extended Russell, leaving McLaren the last option.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli leads by 25 points heading into the Belgian GP after a British GP failure
items.summary: F1 has no race this weekend before the Belgian GP at Spa on July 19; Kimi Antonelli holds 179 points, 25 ahead of George Russell, after finishing outside the points at the British GP won by Leclerc.

items.headline: Scientists capture a mid-ocean ridge tearing open in real time for the first time
items.summary: Instruments on the Southeast Indian Ridge recorded a seafloor-spreading episode from April 2024: the valley floor dropped about 4m, plates pulled apart over a metre, and ~160m cubic metres of lava erupted over 16 days.

items.headline: Euclid telescope finds the two oldest quasars ever observed
items.summary: ESA's Euclid uncovered 31 early-universe quasars, including the two most ancient yet seen, shining when the cosmos was just 670 million years old; the most distant sits at redshift 7.77.

items.headline: Eli Lilly's weight-loss pill outperforms oral semaglutide in a head-to-head trial
items.summary: In the Phase 3 ACHIEVE-3 trial, Lilly's once-daily pill orforglipron beat oral semaglutide on weight loss and blood sugar in type 2 diabetes, cutting HbA1c up to ~2.2% and weight ~9% at the top dose.

items.headline: Researchers eavesdrop on the single neurons that build human sentences
items.summary: Recording individual neurons during unscripted conversation and pairing them with AI language models, scientists found brain cells that encode meaning and grammar in the moment before a person speaks.

fun_fact.headline: Canada has more lakes than any other country on Earth.
fun_fact.body: Canada holds roughly 60% of the world's lakes, more than any other country; broad surveys put its total in the millions and fresh water covers close to 9% of its area.
fun_fact.source: Environment and Climate Change Canada / HydroLAKES analysis

puzzle.title: Counting the Board
puzzle.body: How many squares of any size are in a 4x4 grid of unit squares?
puzzle.approach: Tally squares of each size separately, then add.

word_puzzle.title: Tea for Seven
word_puzzle.body: Spelling Bee: centre T, outer A B E L N O; find the pangram.
word_puzzle.approach: Every word contains T and uses only the seven letters; the pangram uses all seven.
word_puzzle.answer: Pangram NOTABLE; others include BATTLE, BOTTLE, TABLE, TABOO, TALON, TOTAL, BLOAT, NOTE, TENT.

notes: India ran on fallback sources (CNN, Bloomberg): all six primary Indian outlets (The Hindu, Indian Express, Hindustan Times, Times of India, NDTV, Economic Times) were unreachable/crawler-blocked; 3+ retry attempts made. UK News ran on fallback sources (Bloomberg, CNBC, Al Jazeera): BBC and Sky News both unreachable/crawler-blocked; 3+ retry attempts made. Singapore items sourced via Mothership as CNA and The Straits Times block the crawler. All items verified against independent second sources.
